fields.meta_title: Church Landing Page Examples and Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a church landing page from a prompt. See four examples: a visit plan, a small group finder, serve team signups, and prayer requests.
fields.h1: Build a Church Landing Page That Welcomes First-Time Visitors
fields.hero_description: Build a church landing page from one prompt, with every visit plan and signup saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds for Your Church
fields.features_subheading: A church landing page is one page that leads a visitor to one next step. Emergent builds the page and the table behind its forms.
fields.feature_1:
Service times a visitor can act on

Describe your services and what a first Sunday looks like, down to where to park. Emergent builds the page around them, with a visit form under the times. Prompt to change any of it.
fields.feature_2:
Forms that ask what greeters need

List what greeters should know before someone arrives, such as kids' ages or a first service. The app asks only those questions and shows the next one based on each answer.
fields.feature_3:
Every reply kept in one table

The app saves every reply, from visit plans to serve signups, to a database you own. Sort by service or date to see which newcomers still need a call from someone at the church.
fields.feature_4:
The right person hears about it

Name who should hear about each kind of reply: the welcome lead, a group leader, the pastor. The app sends that person an email, Slack message, or in-app alert, then a reminder.
fields.feature_5:
Connected to the tools you already run

The app connects to any tool with an API. A new visitor's answers can go straight into your church management system or email list, with nothing copied over by hand from email.
fields.feature_6:
Your church's domain, your code

Publish on your church's own domain; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep a copy.

fields.tab_content_1:
Kids' ages go to Rosalind before Sunday

A visitor tells Cedar Hollow Community Church which service they will attend, 9:00 or 10:45, and if kids are coming. If so, the app asks their ages and emails welcome lead Rosalind Achebe-Marsh, so a greeter meets them at check-in. In September 18 of 46 families brought kids, the Vantreese family among them.
fields.tab_content_2:
Of 14 groups, Delphine sees the 3 with room

Harrow Lane Church runs 14 small groups, and its finder asks a visitor for a night and a part of town, then shows only matching groups with open spots. Delphine Marchand picked Tuesday on the east side and saw 3 groups. Her request went by email to Keoni Halvorsen, whose group has 4 open spots.
fields.tab_content_3:
Untrained nursery signups reach Mareike before a Sunday

One signup page fills Northgate Chapel's parking, greeting, worship tech, and nursery teams. A nursery signup without the child safety training goes to children's director Mareike Osterhaus before any Sunday is scheduled. Of 38 signups in October, 11 chose nursery and 4 went to Mareike, Callum Ibarra among them.
fields.tab_content_4:
31 of 52 requests stayed with the pastor

Each request on Stonebridge Fellowship's page is marked Pastor only or Prayer team by the person who sends it. A Pastor only request reaches Pastor Ifeoma Adeyemi and no one else; the rest go on the prayer team's list. In October 52 requests came in: 31 stayed with the pastor and 21 went to the prayer team.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Church Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps take a church landing page from one first-time visitor to a live page that tells your welcome team who is coming.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the one visitor it is for
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the one visitor you want this page to reach, such as a family new to town or a neighbor who has never been to a service. Every line on the page should answer what that person would ask before coming.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Put the service times above the fold, with the address and where to park. Nobody planning a first visit should have to scroll to find out when to arrive or which door to use.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Describe a Sunday in plain words: how long the service runs, what people wear, where kids go, and who will say hello at the door. Use two or three photos of your own people instead of stock images.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Choose the one thing a reader should do on this page: plan a visit, join a small group, sign up to serve, or send a prayer request. Give each of the others its own page and link.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the page in one prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your service times into Emergent with the questions you want answered and who should hear about each reply. Emergent builds the page with a row for every answer, and you prompt again to change any of it.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Decide who replies to each new visitor and how soon, even if that is one volunteer. A family that planned a visit should hear from a real person before Sunday, by name, with the time to arrive.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Plan your own visit as a test. Check that the row lands in your table and the email reaches the right person, then publish on your church's domain and share the link in your bulletin and social posts.

faq_plan.q: What is a church landing page?
faq_plan.a: A church landing page is a single page built to get one kind of visitor to take one step, such as planning a first visit or joining a small group. It tells a newcomer when and where each service meets and what a Sunday is like, then asks for that one step, with no menu leading the reader elsewhere.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a church landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe your services, who the page is for, and the step you want visitors to take in one prompt to Emergent's AI landing page builder. Emergent builds the page and a table that saves every reply. Gather your service times and a few photos of your own people first. Then plan a test visit yourself and publish.

faq_plan.q: What should a church landing page include for first-time visitors?
faq_plan.a: It should include the service times, the address and parking, how long a service runs, what happens with kids, and one form to plan a visit. Add a photo of the people a visitor will meet at the door and a line on what to wear. Leave sermon archives and staff bios off the page and link to them instead.

faq_plan.q: Should a church landing page cover one ministry or all of them?
faq_plan.a: One ministry, whenever each ministry asks visitors for a different step. A small group finder and a serve team signup each work better on their own page with their own form. The same idea holds for a nonprofit landing page built around one appeal: one page for one audience and one action, with a link back to the main site.

faq_plan.q: How do I get first-time visitors to plan a visit from a church landing page?
faq_plan.a: Keep the form short: a name, an email, the service they plan to attend, and whether kids are coming. Then tell them what happens next, such as a greeter meeting them at the door. The app Emergent builds saves each plan to a database you own, where your welcome team can see every family before Sunday.

faq_plan.q: What questions belong on a church landing page for volunteer signups?
faq_plan.a: Ask for a name, a phone number or email, the team they want, and which Sundays they can serve. For teams that work with children, ask whether they have finished your church's training; a leader can then follow up before scheduling anyone. Keep sensitive details, such as background check information, off the public form and handle them directly.

faq_plan.q: How do I make a church landing page that more visitors act on?
faq_plan.a: Give the page one job and put that step where a visitor sees it without scrolling. Borrow what works on any high converting landing page. Use a headline that says who the church is for, a short form, a quote from a member who first came as a visitor, and no menu pulling readers away.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep prayer requests private on a church landing page?
faq_plan.a: Let the person sending the request choose who sees it, such as the pastor only or the prayer team, and send each choice to different people. Ask for a first name only, and never show requests on the public page. The app can email the pastor each private request as it arrives, with a reminder if it waits too long.

faq_plan.q: What photos should go on a church landing page?
faq_plan.a: Use photos of your own congregation and building, such as the front door a visitor will walk through and the room where kids go during the service. Ask permission before posting anyone's face, and ask a parent before posting a photo of a child. Skip stock photos: a visitor wants to see the place they are about to walk into.

faq_plan.q: How do I stay in touch with visitors after they use a church landing page?
faq_plan.a: Send a personal note from a named person within a few days of the first visit, then invite them to one more thing, such as a small group or a newcomers' lunch. For people who want regular updates, point them to a newsletter landing page where they sign up for the church's emails. An app built with Emergent can connect to the email tool you already use through its API.

plan.angle: Searchers for a church landing page want examples and a page that turns a website visitor into a person who shows up. The top results are church website galleries, design shots and one Easter page checklist; none shows what happens after someone fills in the form. This page shows four church pages built from a prompt and what each does with a reply: a plan-a-visit page that tells the welcome lead which families bring kids, a small group finder that shows only groups with open spots on the night a visitor picks, a serve team signup that sends untrained nursery volunteers to the children's director first, and a prayer request page where pastor-only requests reach one pastor. Respectful and non-denominational, no theology. Nonprofit giving, event ticketing and Christmas Eve service RSVPs belong to sibling pages and stay out.

Harrow Lane Church runs 14 small groups, a visitor picks a night and a part of town, and the page shows only groups with open spots; Delphine Marchand picked Tuesday on the east side, saw 3 groups, and her request to join went to group leader Keoni Halvorsen, whose group has 4 open spots.

Northgate Chapel's serve team signup lets people pick parking, greeting, worship tech or nursery, and a nursery signup who has not finished the church's child safety training goes to children's director Mareike Osterhaus before any Sunday is scheduled: in October 38 people signed up, 11 chose nursery and 4 of those went to Mareike first, Callum Ibarra among them.

Stonebridge Fellowship's prayer request page lets each person mark a request Pastor only or Prayer team, pastor-only requests reach Pastor Ifeoma Adeyemi alone, and the rest go on the prayer team's list: in October 52 requests came in, 31 pastor only and 21 for the prayer team.
